calendarMirrorModal.title: Sync to Android Calendar
calendarMirrorModal.intro: Calino copies your events into Android's own calendar database — the same one your calendar widget, Wear OS watch and Android Auto read from. Those apps can't see Calino's storage, so this is what makes your events show up in them.
calendarMirrorModal.reliabilityTitle: Why it makes reminders more reliable
calendarMirrorModal.reliabilityP1: On its own, Calino can only schedule a reminder while it's running. Android schedules reminders for events in its calendar whether or not Calino has been opened, so while this is on, Android delivers them and Calino stands down — you won't get two notifications for the same event.
calendarMirrorModal.reliabilityP2: This needs a calendar app installed to actually raise the notification. If you don't have one, Calino says so above and keeps handling reminders itself.
calendarMirrorModal.oneWayItem1: The mirrored calendars are read-only. Calino stays the only thing that writes to your CalDAV server, and nothing you do in another calendar app comes back.
calendarMirrorModal.oneWayItem2: Only calendars you've set to visible are copied.
calendarMirrorModal.oneWayItem3: Turning this off deletes the mirrored calendars again, leaving your other calendars untouched.
calendarMirrorModal.stayingUpToDateP1: About once an hour Calino checks your server in the background, so an event you add on another device gets to your phone and reminds you even if you haven't opened Calino since. Nothing is sent anywhere new — it's the same connection to your own server that the app already uses.
calendarMirrorModal.betaP1: The background check is at the mercy of your phone's battery settings. Xiaomi, Samsung, OPPO, OnePlus and Huawei devices in particular freeze background apps aggressively, and will silently skip it. If your events seem stale, set Calino to No restrictions in Android's battery settings for the app.
calendarMirrorModal.betaP2: If a mirrored calendar doesn't appear in your calendar app, it's usually hidden rather than missing — new calendars often arrive unticked in that app's own list of calendars to display.

section1.heading: 1. Your Data Stays on Your Device
section1.body: Calino is a local-first calendar application. All your calendar events, settings, and preferences are stored locally in your browser using IndexedDB and localStorage. We do not have access to your personal data.

section2.heading: 2. CalDAV Sync (Optional)
section2.intro: Calino can sync with CalDAV servers (like Nextcloud, ownCloud, or other CalDAV-compliant services) you personally configure. When you add a CalDAV account:
section2.item1: Your credentials (username/password) are stored only in your browser's localStorage
section2.item2: Data is transferred directly between your browser and your CalDAV server
section2.item3: We never see or store your credentials on any external server

section3.heading: 3. CORS Proxy (Optional)
section3.intro: If your CalDAV server does not support CORS, you can optionally use a CORS proxy to enable browser access.
section3.hostedProxyIntro: We provide a public CORS proxy at {{proxy}}. If you use this option:
section3.item1: We can see your IP address, country, and the full URL of each request (which can sometimes include parts of your account path, depending on your CalDAV server)
section3.item2: We cannot see your password or calendar event data
section3.item3: Credentials are sent in the Authorization header (not logged)
section3.item4: Request/response bodies containing calendar data are not logged
section3.thirdPartyBody: The same principles apply — the proxy operator sees connection metadata but not your credentials or calendar content.
section3.maxPrivacy: For maximum privacy, add CORS headers directly to your CalDAV server instead of using a proxy.

section4.heading: 4. Cookies & Local Storage
section4.item2: CalDAV account credentials, obfuscated with a key stored in the app itself. This protects against casual inspection of localStorage (e.g. another site or extension accessing it by mistake), but is not strong encryption against someone with access to both the app source and your browser storage.
section4.outro: We do not use tracking cookies, analytics, or third-party services that collect personal information.

section5.heading: 5. No Account Required
section5.body: Calino does not require registration or an account. You can use the app immediately without providing any personal information.

section6.body: If you have questions about this privacy policy, please contact:
